title: perf(hip): optimize GDN verify kernels with LDS-only barriers and enable batched commit under STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1
body:
## Summary

Optimizes the Gated Delta Net (GDN) speculative-verify forward and commit kernels in `src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.cu` while preserving **100% bit-for-bit output and state parity**:

1. **Enable 2-launch batched `gdn_commit_layers` when `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1` (`verify_kernels.cu:1073`):**
   - `gdn_commit_layers` previously checked `(sp && sp[0] == '1')` (`STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1`) and returned `false`, forcing `verify.cpp:2419` to fall back to **72 per-layer kernel launches** (`gdn_conv_commit` + `gdn_state_replay_kernel` across 36 GDN layers) instead of the 2-launch 36-layer batched commit (`gdn_conv_commit_layers_kernel` + `gdn_step_commit_layers_kernel`).
   - Because `gdn_step_commit_layers_kernel` and `gdn_state_replay_kernel` share the exact same `32 × 4` column-split state layout and `red[0..3][col_local]` reduction order, their committed states are **100% bitwise identical** (`gdn_parity` Section 6: 8 `n_keep` cases × 5 layers, 0 mismatches).
   - Notably, `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1` is enabled by default on `gfx1151` (`Strix Halo`) in `src/core/arch_defaults.cpp`, so `gfx1151` was silently falling back to 72 per-layer commit launches on every verify window.
   - `STRATA_GDN_COMMIT_SPLIT=0` and `STRATA_DBG_GDN=1` remain available as explicit per-layer commit overrides, and `gdn_parity.cpp` now fails if `gdn_commit_layers` is unexpectedly skipped when neither override is set.

2. **LDS-only workgroup barriers (`vk_sync_lds()`) in GDN verify kernels (`verify_kernels.cu:37`):**
   - On RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`) and RDNA3 (`gfx11xx`/`gfx1030`), `__syncthreads()` compiles to a full workgroup memory fence (`s_wait_loadcnt 0x0; s_wait_storecnt 0x0; s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx12`), draining all in-flight global memory loads and invalidating the shader engine's L1 vector cache at every LDS synchronization point (4× per token in `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel`, 5× per token in `gdn_step_split_kernel`, 3× per token in `gdn_step_commit_body`).
   - Since inter-thread communication in `gdn_conv_l2_body`, `gdn_step_commit_body`, `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel`, `gdn_step_split_kernel`, `gdn_state_replay_kernel`, and `gdn_out_norm_kernel` goes strictly through `__shared__` memory (LDS), `vk_sync_lds()` uses `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12` and `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx11`/`gfx1030` (falling back to `__syncthreads()` on CUDA and other targets).

3. **Prologue state-load ordering and unified next-token prefetch in `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel` (`verify_kernels.cu:328`):**
   - Issuing the 32 per-thread state loads (`s[0..31]`) before the initial `sk[0]`/`sq[0]` LDS store allows `vk_sync_lds()` at `t = 0` to overlap all 32 global state loads with the first barrier.
   - Unifying the `rg == 0` (`sk`) and `rg == 1` (`sq`) next-token prefetch under a single predicate (`load_kq`) overlaps the global load of token `t + 1`'s `k`/`q` and token `t`'s `v`/`z` with the 32-FMA `kv` and `o` loops while reducing register pressure by **4–7 VGPRs** across all four `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel` instantiations.

4. **Double-buffered 3-barrier `gdn_step_split_kernel` (`verify_kernels.cu:417`):**
   - `gdn_step_split_kernel<true>` previously used single-buffered `sk[S]`, `sq[S]`, and `red[RG][GS_COLS]`, requiring **5 barriers per token** and stalling on `ht` global loads inside the barrier pair.
   - Double-buffering `sk[2][S]` and `sq[2][S]` with separate `red_kv[RG][GS_COLS]` and `red_o[RG][GS_COLS]` (LDS `1536 B -> 3072 B`, preserving full 16-wave / 4-CTA-per-WGP occupancy) reduces the loop to **3 `vk_sync_lds()` barriers per token** and overlaps next-token `k`/`q` global loads with the 32-FMA `kv` dot product.

---

## Root Cause & RED / GREEN Verification

On `origin/main` (`477ac13c`), running `gdn_parity` with `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1` skipped Section 6 (`gdn_commit_layers == per-layer commit`) because `gdn_commit_layers` returned `false`. With the tightened assertion in `src/kernels/gdn_parity.cpp`:

- **RED (`origin/main` `verify_kernels.cu` + `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1 ./gdn_parity`):**
  ```text
  gdn_ab_multi T=1..8 == fused_gdn_ab        bitwise (8 cases)
  gdn_step_norm_multi T=1..8 == single-token bitwise (47 cases)
  gdn_commit_layers == per-layer commit      *** NO (unexpectedly skipped) ***

  gdn: 1 failures
  ```
- **GREEN (this PR + `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1 ./gdn_parity`):**
  ```text
  gdn_ab_multi T=1..8 == fused_gdn_ab        bitwise (8 cases)
  gdn_step_norm_multi T=1..8 == single-token bitwise (47 cases)
  gdn_commit_layers == per-layer commit      bitwise (8 cases, 5 layers)

  gdn: 0 failures
  ```
- `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=0 ./gdn_parity`, `STRATA_GDN_COMMIT_SPLIT=0 ./gdn_parity`, `./verify_batch_parity --selftest`, `./spec_verify_parity`, and `./arch_defaults_test` all pass with 0 failures.

---

## Code Object Resource Usage (`gfx1201`, `llvm-readobj --notes`)

| Kernel (`gfx1201`) | `origin/main` (VGPR / SGPR / LDS / Spills) | This PR (VGPR / SGPR / LDS / Spills) |
|---|---|---|
| `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel<true, false>` | `89 / 32 / 6160 B / 0` | **`83 / 32 / 6160 B / 0`** (`-6 VGPRs`) |
| `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel<true, true>` | `92 / 38 / 6160 B / 0` | **`88 / 38 / 6160 B / 0`** (`-4 VGPRs`) |
| `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel<false, false>` | `168 / 38 / 6160 B / 0` | **`162 / 34 / 6160 B / 0`** (`-6 VGPRs, -4 SGPRs`) |
| `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel<false, true>` | `173 / 38 / 6160 B / 0` | **`166 / 38 / 6160 B / 0`** (`-7 VGPRs`) |
| `gdn_step_split_kernel<true>` | `140 / 30 / 1536 B / 0` | **`142 / 30 / 3072 B / 0`** (`5 -> 3` barriers/tok) |
| `gdn_step_commit_layers_kernel` | `141 / 28 / 1024 B / 0` | **`141 / 28 / 1024 B / 0`** (LDS-only barriers) |

Compiled cleanly with zero errors across HIP targets (`gfx1100, gfx1101, gfx1102, gfx1103, gfx1151, gfx1200, gfx1201`) and CUDA targets (`sm_75, sm_89, sm_100, sm_120`).

---

title: STRATA_RAM_ADAPT: copy an incoming expert out of its stage buffer instead of a second file read
body:
## Title STRATA_RAM_ADAPT: copy an incoming expert out of its stage buffer instead of a second file read Issue: follow-up to #1837 / #1838 (in main as d7298883) ## Summary On #1838 you measured no gain on the bench and a decode loss. We reproduced it on the `strata_bench.py` normal suite (short chat −3.4% with `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8`). The option only pays off once the RAM copy has followed a conversation for a while, and every move cost a file re-read on the decode thread (~0.77 ms, 8 moves per window), so a short request ended before the moves paid back. This change makes a move a memcpy out of the stage buffer the demand read just filled (~0.1 ms). Result: the short bench no longer loses (+3.2% decode, prefill unchanged), and the long sessions this option is for gain clearly: **+33.8% decode on 120 ShareGPT requests** and +19.2% on a 47-request session, with cumulative time down 23% / 13%. ## What changed - `src/core/expert_source.cpp`, `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`: `replace_resident_staged()` moves a pair when the incoming blob is still in a finished stage buffer; the buffer is held under `stage_mu_` during the copy; same Foresight hold and between-window checks as `replace_resident()`. Counter `ram_staged()`. - `src/program/generate.cpp`: the `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT` loop tries the staged copy first for every ranked pair (up to one per layer per window); `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=` now caps only the pairs that still need a file read (1 is enough). Pair selection, thresholds and the stage buffers' size and reuse are unchanged; still opt-in. The stats line counts staged moves. - `tests/core/file_expert_source_test.cpp`: a staged move writes the exact bytes, refuses an unstaged or invalid pair and leaves the other experts untouched (pinned and pageable). - `docs/DETAILS.md`: the `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT` entry. ## Extra Notes v0.1.45 + this commit, RTX 3060 12 GB, IQ2_XS, 3769 VRAM expert slots, `--resident-budget-gib 20.5` (~74% of the experts outside the GPU), NVMe. Fresh process per run, `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=1`. | Workload | Decode tok/s
OFF → ON | Prefill tok/s
OFF → ON | SSD expert reads / token
OFF → ON | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `strata_bench.py` normal suite (15 req., short) | 38.7 → 39.9 (+3.2%, no loss) | 446 → 445 (−0.2%) | 15.9 → 9.7 (−39%) | | ShareGPT, 30 conversations × 4 turns (120 req.) | 36.6 → 48.9 (**+33.8%**) | 119 → 142 (+19%) | 22.9 → 4.5 (−80%) | | English 47-request session (in the kit) | 43.7 → 52.1 (**+19.2%**) | 277 → 292 (+5%) | 12.6 → 0.9 (−93%) | Runs were OFF, ON, OFF; OFF in the table is the run after ON. The OFF run before ON gave 38.3 / 36.5 / 44.1 decode tok/s, within 1% of the one after. ![ShareGPT 120 requests: decode ms per token, SSD expert reads per token and cumulative time saved, OFF vs STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SanghunYun/Strata/ram-adapt-replay/charts/sharegpt120.png) In the long session ON is faster from the first requests and stays there; the cumulative saving grows to 9% after 10 requests, 16% after 30 and 23% after 120. Paired per-request decode-time ratio (ON / OFF): ShareGPT 0.747 (95% CI 0.734–0.761), English 0.839 (0.819–0.861). One run per arm. With a RAM budget below the experts outside the GPU the #669 lend-region warning is printed in every run; that is the case this option is for. Replay: requests, the ShareGPT builder, replay/summary scripts, the exact engine arguments and our per-request numbers are at https://github.com/SanghunYun/Strata/tree/ram-adapt-replay Tests: CUDA sm86 Release `file_expert_source_test --rotation-gpu` passes with the new case. HIP gfx1100 Release (ROCm 7.10): engine and test build and link, host-side `file_expert_source_test` passes; no AMD GPU inference.

title: Add a gfx1101 hipBLASLt table (RX 7800 XT, hipBLASLt 1.5.0): +14/+52/+72% prompt at 1K/8K/24K
body:
`docs/AMD_HIP.md` says gfx1101 has no hipBLASLt table ("make one with Tuning table and compare the prompt speed with
and without it"). This adds one, calibrated on an RX 7800 XT with the hipBLASLt shipped in the 0.1.44.1 Windows HIP
package (version 100500), plus the measurements.

## What changes

- **Adds** `tools/hip/gfx1101-hipblaslt-100500.txt` (70 rows). Setup picks it only for a gfx1101 card whose installed
  hipBLASLt reports 100500, by the existing `hipblaslt_table()` file-name rule; no code changes.
- **Adds** `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-rx-7800-xt-hipblaslt-100500/`: calibration method and script, per-row
  timings, launch configs and per-run prompt-speed data.
- **Edits** `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: the "gfx1101 has none" sentence and one entry in "Shipped tables".
- **Leaves alone**: the engine, setup, every other table. Other cards and other hipBLASLt versions are unaffected.

## Measured

Prebuilt Windows HIP engine 0.1.44.1, same `strata.exe` in both arms, only `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING` differs.
Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, 32K context, fresh prompts, medians of 3:

| Prompt tokens | Prompt tok/s without → with | Decode tok/s | TTFT s |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,060 | 161.7 → 184.5 (+14%) | 28.2 → 29.7 | 6.60 → 5.79 |
| 8,041 | 335.1 → 510.8 (+52%) | 29.6 → 29.0 | 24.07 → 15.80 |
| 24,054 | 404.6 → 695.2 (+72%) | 29.9 → 29.2 | 59.51 → 34.67 |

Per GEMM against plain hipBLAS: median 6.45x, geometric mean 5.80x, 0.81x–15.9x; all 70 rows pass the upstream

title: serve: read conversation-cache log backlogs without dropping events
body:
When unread engine output exceeds 1 MiB, the cache observer jumps to the last MiB and permanently misses earlier cache events. Read from the committed cursor through a captured EOF in chunks of at most 1 MiB, advancing the cursor only through complete newline-terminated records. The observer now scans the captured unread backlog, so catch-up time scales with unread bytes. It avoids allocating the whole backlog: each read is bounded, with unfinished-line storage proportional to the longest line. It does not impose a line-length discard policy.

## Title

Resolves #3045

## Summary

`PleReader::open()` can block forever during cleanup before submitting any reads: slab allocation failure publishes a nonzero slot count with no free slots, and failed reopen inherits the previous slot count after close cleared the free slots. Both paths wait for completions that cannot exist. Failed initialization now returns the existing error, closes the file and permits a later valid open.

## What changed

- Publish `max_inflight` only after the slab and free-slot list are initialized.
- Reset `max_inflight` when closing the reader.
- Add a Linux CPU-only lifecycle test with caller-thread and I/O-worker cases. Link-time `posix_memalign` wrapping injects a one-shot ENOMEM without adding production fault-injection settings. CTest timeouts turn the former hangs into bounded failures.

Successful row reads, page-straddling rows, close with outstanding reads, repeated close and read-after-recovery are covered. The I/O scheduling, cache, kernels, row bytes, defaults and public API remain unchanged.

## Validation

Linux x86_64, GCC 14.2.0; isolated branch from directly fetched upstream main `477ac13cbe8e582c20484871ce459d20d82df09d`.

- CMake CPU build with `STRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON` and `STRATA_WERROR=ON`: built `ple_reader_lifecycle_test` and `direct_file_async_test`.
- CTest: all 7 selected tests passed (6 lifecycle cases and existing DirectFile async test). Successful reads are compared byte-for-byte against an independent fixture pattern.
- Compiled the same lifecycle test against unchanged upstream: both normal-read controls passed; allocation and reopen cases timed out after 2 seconds in both caller and threaded modes (4 timeouts).
- `git diff --check` passed.

Draft; no review requested. AGENTS.md requires builds of every affected backend before review. Full CUDA/HIP/SYCL engine builds have not been run; HIP and SYCL compilers are unavailable here. Fixes #3033. After a refused conversation-cache park, `/metrics` and the Monitor card could still report the old occupancy even when the engine said it had evicted every parked entry. The observer now applies the remaining count from that refusal and represents missing values as unknown rather than displaying stale values.

## What changed

- Parse physical-RAM refusal counts; report zero bytes when that path explicitly says no entries remain. Do not add its per-attempt eviction count to a cumulative total: budget eviction may have happened earlier.
- Invalidate occupancy and cumulative eviction values that unsuccessful parking cannot establish. Superseded-copy and minimum-length messages retain their known count but do not invent a byte count. A subsequent authoritative log summary restores numeric values.
- Keep successful park/restore counters and the last successful switch unchanged. Unknown values are JSON `null`; the Monitor shows a dash and hides the corresponding occupancy bar. The contract is documented in `docs/DETAILS.md`.
- Add eight regression tests covering empty/partial eviction, budget and allocation refusals, legacy log format, partial lines, run resets, recovery, HTTP metrics and the card's unknown-to-known transition.

The patch changes only the Python observer, its web display, tests and documentation. Native cache policy, inference, engine log formats and defaults are unchanged.

## Validation

- Red/green: the new cases fail against the unmodified observer and pass after the fix; the targeted cache-card class passes all 11 tests.
- Replayed the preserved failure log: `parked=38` becomes `parked=0`, `bytes=0`; the unreported cumulative eviction count becomes unknown until a full summary supplies it.
- Python 3.12 on Windows: `python -m unittest serve.test_monitor serve.test_server serve.test_web_sampling serve.test_parallel serve.test_slots serve.test_prometheus -v` — 426 tests, 422 passed, 4 existing platform skips (three signal tests and one symlink-privilege test).
- Python compilation, `node --check serve/web/app.js`, and `git diff --check` pass. Ruff reports the same three pre-existing `serve/server.py` findings as the base and no new findings; the modified test file is clean.
- All runtime checks use a local mock engine. No live model service was restarted or changed; native GPU inference was not rerun for this observer-only change.

Related: #2962 concerns pressure-release policy. This PR fixes observation of existing logs and does not adopt that policy.

title: fix(Metal): the prompt path no longer kills the engine on prompts > 6…
body:
fix(Metal): the prompt path no longer kills the engine on prompts > 64 tokens

Addresses #2671 - the Metal failure reported there (same machine family, M1 Max 64 GB; the
follow-up comment's diagnosis, `!m.borrowed` inside `Prefill::relayout`, matches what I measured).

## What this changes

On Metal, every prompt over 64 tokens kills the engine, in two ways:

1. a ~1.6k-token prompt: `lending the prompt path its slots failed: ... at most 0`, exit 1
   (the guard inside `Prefill::relayout`, as #2671 diagnosed);
2. a 10,797-token prompt: the read completes, then SIGABRT `a copy touches a device allocation
   of 21298.5 MB that was given back` inside `ExpertCache::fill_slot_queued`, exit -6. The Metal
   arena purges host allocations >= 32 MB (`metal/src/engine/window.cpp` `stream_arena` ->
   `purge_device_allocations(32<<20)`), and the post-read refill writes into that purged region
   through the slots the lend loop marked.

One root cause under both: on Metal the prompt's buffers live in the Metal arena (`window_ensure`),
not in the host region the host code believes it is borrowing, and the Metal window never reads the
host residency table. So the relayout has nothing to re-layout, and the lend has nothing to lend.

- `Prefill::relayout`: on Metal, a successful no-op that keeps the larger chunk count (the Metal
  buffers never shrink; a large `chunk()` is one `run()` per segment).
- the `lend` lambda: the slot-marking loop is guarded out, so `p.lent` stays empty and the refill
  after the read is a no-op instead of writing to purged host memory. `p.lent_chunk = want_p` stays.

## What this leaves alone

Every added line is inside a `STRATA_GPU_METAL` / `!STRATA_GPU_METAL` guard: the CUDA / HIP / SYCL
branch is the untouched pre-fix source, byte-identical by construction. The startup line "the prompt
path borrows N CUDA0 cache slots" still logs (cosmetic on Metal) and the sizing arithmetic is
untouched. No new flags, no behaviour change on any other backend.

## How I checked

Apple M1 Max 64 GB, macOS 27.0, engine 0.1.45-metal, test arena 8 GB (`STRATA_METAL_ARENA_GB=8`):

- pre-fix repro, both modes, deterministic: ~1.6k-token prompt -> "at most 0" exit 1;
  10,797-token prompt -> "given back" SIGABRT exit -6.
- post-fix: 4,643-token prompt -> prefill 85.3 tok/s, 512 tokens generated at 9.3 tok/s, engine
  alive after; 10,797-token prompt -> prefill 179.8 tok/s, 512 generated at 6.9 tok/s, engine alive
  after. Log over both: no "given back", no "at most 0", no lending error. `/health`: loaded.
- `ninja -C build-metal` full build 0 errors; `ctest` 1/1 (`runtime_hello`); `gr_parity` ALL PASS
  (prepared planes bitwise, rel-L2 <= 3.4e-08 on the rest); `prompt_parity` ALL PASS.

**Not checked:** the CUDA / HIP / SYCL builds cannot be compiled on a Mac (no toolchains). Per
AGENTS.md a build per backend is the check before merge; the guard makes the non-Metal branch the
untouched source, but I cannot claim the builds, only the construction.

## Numbers on the shipping configuration

Same machine, the default run (`run-iq3_s.sh`, IQ3_S, expert arena ~32.5 GB, 256K context):
prefill ~220 tok/s, decode ~20 tok/s, and long prompts complete with the engine staying up. These
are read off the server's own logs during normal use, not a controlled benchmark; the 8 GB-arena
numbers above are the controlled ones (the small arena is what makes its prefill slower).

title: docs: add a Windows Strix Halo (gfx1151) deployment guide
body:
## What this adds

`docs/STRIX_HALO_WINDOWS.md`, a companion to `docs/STRIX_HALO.md` for the Windows
path. `STRIX_HALO.md` documents the Linux build and the release notes mark the
Windows one as untested on a Strix Halo; this document records a working Windows
deployment on the same hardware, with measured numbers and the traps that cost
time.

## Why

The Windows HIP build has carried gfx1151 code since 0.1.40, but no Windows
configuration was documented. Three findings are worth having in writing:

- `--mmap-experts` is the single biggest lever on Windows: the default resident
  expert arena pins 46.84 GiB into host memory, which WDDM counts against the
  process GPU budget, leaving 2.25 GiB free and squeezing the expert cache to 320
  slots (28.0 tok/s). Dropping the arena for mmap over the GGUF shards takes the
  cache to 24,576 slots and decode to 37.7 tok/s (+35%).
- `STRATA_SH_STREAM=0`: the switch is on by default on gfx1151 and pays on Linux,
  but costs 13% here on Windows (34.1 -> 39.6 tok/s), matching issue #816.
- `--kv-streaming` is a `setup` option, not an engine option, and KV streaming is
  not usable at 128K on this machine at all while `--mmap-experts` is available.

## Impact

Documentation only; no code or engine change. Windows Strix Halo users get a
configuration that reaches about 40 tok/s on IQ3_S (39.6 Chinese, 42.3 English)
at 128K, within a few percent of the Linux reference (42.8 in `STRIX_HALO.md`
section 6), and 34.0 tok/s at the model's native 256K context.

## What was checked

- Every number is a median of three runs on one machine, and the doc names the
  engine build for each row (0.1.41 for the tuning rows, 0.1.45 for the context
  and version rows).
- The 0.1.43 -> 0.1.45 upgrade was A/B'd and changes nothing here (34.0 against
  32.6), consistent with the release notes: the default speed-ups in 0.1.42 and
  0.1.43 are CUDA and RDNA4 only, and 0.1.45 states it did not run on Windows.
  gfx1151's default switch count does go from 17 to 18, the addition being
  `STRATA_TOPK_REG_MIN_BLOCKS`.
- The 128K -> 256K change was A/B'd back to back: 32.6 at 256K against 30.8 at
  128K, i.e. flat, with the expert cache unchanged at 24,576 slots and about
  1.8 GiB of VRAM taken by the KV. 262,144 is the native trained length, so no
  rope scaling is involved.
- `not measured` is used wherever a value was not taken rather than estimated.
- Section 3.5 lists two upstream gfx1151 switches (`STRATA_PF_F16`,
  `STRATA_REFILL_PARTS`) and the remaining Linux-tuned defaults as leads that were
  not confirmed: the first A/B attempt was invalidated by page-cache drift (the
  engine restarts took 57 s, 70 s and 141 s to fill the expert cache), so they are
  listed as open rather than claimed.

title: setup: --skip-gguf-sha256, for a model file that is another build of the model setup pins
body:
## What this adds

One opt-in setup flag: `python setup.py --skip-gguf-sha256`. With it, `verify_sha256`
compares neither the pinned size nor the pinned SHA-256 of the model files (GGUF shards
and the mmproj), warns with the size on disk next to the pinned size and the pinned
hash prefix, and keeps the file instead of deleting it. Without the flag the default
path is byte-identical to v0.1.45.

## Why

We often want to run a variant of a model Strata officially supports instead of the
pinned repository file: for example huihui-ai's
[Huihui-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-abliterated-v2-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-abliterated-v2-GGUF)
instead of unsloth's [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF)
(the same model, refusal answers edited out, re-sharded: same architecture, so the
engine runs it, but neither the file sizes nor the hashes match the pins in `setup.py`).
Today setup deletes such a file and stops, and the only workaround is editing
`verify_sha256` out of `setup.py` by hand. Same symptom from #2635 and #2346, where a
repository moved its file after the pin was taken; see also #1979 and #2842.

## What it leaves alone

- The ready-made engine keeps its own separate switch (`STRATA_SKIP_SHA256`,
  `check_engine_digest`); neither one implies the other, and a test pins that.
- `check_shards` still reads the GGUF headers, so a truncated or incompatible file is
  refused even with the flag.
- A skipped file's `.done` mark records `sha256 skipped (N bytes)`, so a later run
  without the flag hashes it again and re-arms the normal check.
- ModelScope's published-hash check, the Vulkan SDK archive and `metal/setup_mac.py`
  keep verifying as before (the Mac path does not take the flag yet).

## How I checked

- New tests in `tools/test_setup_unsloth.py`: the skip accepts a different build and
  keeps the file, skips the hashing, re-hashes a mark from an earlier skipped run, and
  `STRATA_SKIP_SHA256=1` alone does not relax the model-file check; one end-to-end test
  shows the flag reaching every pinned model file (`main()` with `--skip-gguf-sha256`).
- All 41 `tools/test_setup_*.py` suites pass on this branch, except
  `test_setup_engine_hash` (2) and `test_setup_golden` (8), which fail identically on a
  clean `477ac13c` in the same checkout (verified with the branch's changes stashed).
- Docs: one line in `docs/INSTALL.md` and the `docs/DETAILS.md` option list, plus a
  `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` entry for "setup says a model file has the wrong SHA-256,
  or the wrong size" that spells out the two separate switches.

body:
bench: community report, RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GiB (Windows 11, 32 GB RAM), Q2_0, engine 0.1.45

Adds `bench/results/2026-10-18-community-rtx-4060-laptop-gpu-qwen3-8-flash-next-q2-0/`: the README the
suite wrote, `results.json` per request and the engine log excerpt. I added a "Notes from the author"
section for the build's provenance, what was not tested, the long-context figures below, and one
measurement the suite does not cover. Nothing else in the tree is touched.

Why it may be useful: **this is the smallest VRAM tier in `bench/results` so far** — there is no single
8 GiB card (the smallest existing entry is a 12 GiB RTX 3060, then 16 and 24 GiB), and 8 GiB is the tier
where the expert cache holds about 9% of the (layer, expert) pairs. `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` also asks for
"a host with 32 GB of RAM or less" because "the expert file tier and the resident mode depend on how much
of the model fits in RAM"; this is such a host (31.7 GiB), on Windows rather than Linux.

Suite medians (3 runs each, temperature 0, thinking off, the install's own configuration):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| short chat decode | **30.5 tok/s** (22.9-44.1, n=9), first token 1.10 s |
| 4K fresh prompt | **220.1 tok/s**, first token 18.33 s |
| 16K fresh prompt | **220.4 tok/s**, first token 72.97 s — no decay from 4K to 16K |
| agent session, follow-up turns | decode **23.1 tok/s** (7.3-33.7, n=15), first token 16.21 s, conversation-cache hit 68.6% |

**Long context, from daily use rather than the suite** (the suite stops at 16K). This install also runs an
agent client against the same Q2_0 server; its engine log covers ten days and 1,932 requests with thinking
on and the client's own sampling, so it is not the suite's protocol:

- the longest prompt carried **113,621 tokens** (112,781 reused from the conversation cache + 840 read) at
  99.5 prompt tok/s, and generated 3,175 tokens at 24.5 tok/s decode
- 88 requests with a 64K-120K prompt: prompt median 47.0 tok/s, decode median 24.0 tok/s
- 27 requests above 96K: decode median 23.9 tok/s, i.e. no decay against the 21.2 tok/s median of the
  1,072 requests above 32K
- the longest single generation was 64,879 tokens (from a 649-token prompt) at 16.2 tok/s

So context is not what limits this machine: the KV cache keeps 20,480 of 131,072 cells per QSA layer in
VRAM with about 0.84 GiB in pinned RAM, and the conversation cache reuses most of a long prompt.

The one thing I would look at: decode here tracks how much of the expert set fits in RAM when the server
starts. Same box, same model (Flash-Next IQ2_XS), same settings, two runs on the same day: a RAM
complement of 10.53 GiB of the 31.03 GiB the VRAM cache does not hold (34%) gave a decode median of
15.5 tok/s; 16.93 GiB (55%) gave 21.6 tok/s. Only the free RAM at startup differed (a clean boot versus a
session with other work loaded).

Not tested in the suite: prompts above 16K (covered above from daily use), `--clients` concurrency,
vision, a layer split, a long soak, and any non-Windows host.

Note: the suite needed two local fixes to `tools/strata_bench.py` to run here (`port` never assigned; the
`CMakeLists.txt` read without an encoding on a Windows whose ANSI code page is not UTF-8). Those are the
sibling pull request; the measurements are unaffected.

title: perf(hip): optimize EXPDEC routed-expert kernels and enable by default on gfx12
body:
## Summary

Optimize the grouped native routed-expert decode kernels (`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`) for RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`), enable `EXPDEC` (`expdec_gu_kernel` and `expdec_down_kernel` on `Q2_0`) by default on `gfx12`, and enable `expdec_bench` on HIP builds.

### Changes

1. **Fix HIP `__launch_bounds__(256, MINB)` wave-occupancy mapping on `expdec_gu_kernel` (`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`)**:
   - On CUDA, `__launch_bounds__(256, MINB)` specifies `MINB` blocks per SM (`4` blocks = $\le 64$ registers). On HIP (`amd_hip_runtime.h`), the second argument of `__launch_bounds__(max_threads, min_blocks)` maps directly to `amdgpu_waves_per_eu(min_blocks)` (waves per SIMD, not blocks per WGP). Since a 256-thread CTA has 8 waves = 2 waves/SIMD on RDNA3/RDNA4, `MINB = 4` requested only 4 waves/SIMD (allowing up to 256 VGPRs), so `expdec_gu_kernel<16..18, 1, 4>` compiled to **`222–223 VGPRs`** on `gfx1201` (capping occupancy at 6 waves/SIMD = 3 CTAs/WGP instead of 8 waves/SIMD = 4 CTAs/WGP).
   - Map the second `__launch_bounds__` argument to `MINB * 2` on HIP (`8` waves/SIMD for `MINB = 4`), dropping `gfx1201` register usage to **`171–187 VGPRs`** (`0` spills, $\le 192$ VGPRs = **4 CTAs/WGP** across `IQ2_XXS`, `IQ2_XS`, `IQ3_XXS`, and `IQ3_S`).

2. **Vectorize `ed_stage_entry` in `expdec_gu_kernel` and `expdec_down_kernel`**:
   - Previously, `ed_stage_entry<XB, HALVES>` looped over `w = tid; w < XB * 9; w += 256`, executing 3 integer divisions by 9 (`w / 9`), 3 intra-warp divergent `if (j == 0)` branches, and 3 scattered 4-byte `ds_store_b32` stores per thread per staged entry.
   - Because `XB <= 80 <= 128` (`ED_XB = 80`, `ED_HB = 20`), map the 256 threads directly as 128 thread-pairs `(k = tid >> 1, h = tid & 1)` where each active pair loads one 16-byte half-block (`int4`) and writes a single 16-byte `ds_store_b128` to `s_u`, while `tid < XB` writes `s_ds[c * XB + tid]` with zero loops, zero `/ 9` divisions, and zero intra-warp branch divergence.

3. **LDS-only barriers (`iq_sync_lds()`) and elided first-pass pre-staging barriers**:
   - Add `iq_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`, `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on other HIP targets, `__syncthreads()` on CUDA) in `stage_iq_grid`, `native_down_multi_kernel`, `expdec_gu_kernel`, and `expdec_down_kernel`, avoiding `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` L0 vector-cache invalidations and global load-queue drains (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0`).
   - Guard the pre-staging barrier inside `for (int e = e0; e < e1; ...)` with `if (g > (int) blockIdx.y || e > e0) iq_sync_lds();` so the first pass (`g == blockIdx.y && e == e0`, which covers all `T <= 4` decode groups when `gridDim.y == cap_groups`) skips a redundant barrier.

4. **Enable `EXPDEC` (`STRATA_EXPDEC=1`, `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN=1`) by default on `gfx12` and enable `expdec_bench` on HIP**:
   - Default `expdec_on()` and `expdec_down_on()` to `1` on `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` (`expdec_default_gfx12()`) when `STRATA_EXPDEC` / `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN` are unset (`STRATA_EXPDEC=0` or `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN=0` turns them off; non-`gfx12` architectures remain unchanged).
   - Gate `expdec_note` stderr logging on explicit `STRATA_EXPDEC=1`.
   - Enable the `expdec_bench` target on HIP builds in `CMakeLists.txt` and map `cudaDevAttrMemoryClockRate` / `cudaDevAttrGlobalMemoryBusWidth` in `include/strata/hip_compat/cuda_runtime.h`.
   - Extend `iq_multi_parity` (`check_grouped`) to verify bitwise equality of both `multi` (`EXPDEC=0`) and `expdec` (`EXPDEC=1, EXPDEC_DOWN=1, EXPDEC_D20=1`) against the reference per-entry kernels across all format pairs.

---

## Validation & Benchmarks (`gfx1201`, AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700)

### 1. Bitwise Parity & Multi-Arch Compilation
- `./build-copilot-hip/iq_multi_parity`: `0 failures` across all 18 `iq_mmvq` checks, 24 `native_expert_grouped` checks (testing both `multi` and `expdec` against `old`), and 3 `q8_1 finite` checks.
- `./build-copilot-hip/expdec_bench 150 0 20 18/20,21/20,22/20,18/42,21/42,22/42 def,dec,dec:w1 real`: `identical` (`0 choice comparisons differ`) across all 6 format pairs and `T = 1..4`.

title: native_dense: STRATA_HC_Q8 uploads only the stage's own Q8_0 rows on a trimmed layer split
body:
## Title
Issue: none found (searched "HC_Q8"). Related: #2427, a different leak on a split, in other lines.

## Summary
On a layer split with `--trim-stage-weights` (or `STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1`) and `STRATA_HC_Q8` on, the loop in `src/core/native_dense.cpp` that attaches the GGUF's Q8_0 hyper-connection rows does not skip other stages' layers. A trimmed stage still has their table entries (metadata only), so every trimmed card uploads the Q8_0 rows of all 48 layers and reads only its own: 0.63 GiB per card on the rig below, 0.15-0.18 GiB with this change.

## What changed
`src/core/native_dense.cpp`, +2 lines: the loop skips a tensor when `outside(name) || !in_range(name)`, the filter the upload loop above it uses. `in_range` does the work here (stage trim sets it through `set_layer_range`; the bf16-pack quantize loop below already checks it). No value changes: each stage reads the same rows as before.

It applies only where all three hold: `STRATA_HC_Q8` is on (setup writes `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` for CUDA UD-* installs; HIP gfx12 turns it on by default), stage trim is on, and the `--native` GGUF itself stores Q8_0 hyper-connection rows (the UD-* files). A bf16 pack's rows come from the quantize loop, which already filters. CUDA0 is trimmed only with an explicit `--layer-split`; the later stages are also trimmed under `auto`, because their weights load after the split search. Without stage trim, `set_layer_range` never runs and `in_range` passes every layer, so nothing changes: the code path is the same, and with the fix and no trim each card still loads 0.63 GiB (I did not run 0.1.45 without trim, and the no-trim tokens are not compared).

## Extra Notes
Measured on 4x RTX 3090 24 GB (sm_86), CUDA 13.0, setup.py release flags, v0.1.45 (`477ac13c`) with and without this commit. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS (`--native` GGUF + pack), `--layer-split 12,25,37 --resident-experts --expert-cache auto --expert-profile <profile> --prefill 512 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <draft> --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 28672 --ple-io ram --batch 16`; env `STRATA_HC_Q8=1 STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1 STRATA_KV_PREFETCH=1 STRATA_NAN_GUARD=0` (the last one turns off a default). All experts are resident in the two trimmed arms; without trim 87 %.

| | trim, 0.1.45 | trim, + fix | no trim, + fix |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `STRATA_HC_Q8=1: ... GiB` (engine line), CUDA0/1/2/3 | 0.63 / 0.63 / 0.63 / 0.63 | 0.16 / 0.18 / 0.16 / 0.15 | 0.63 / 0.63 / 0.63 / 0.63 |
| free before the expert cache, GiB, CUDA0/1/2/3 | 16.01 / 16.27 / 16.43 / 15.25 | 16.60 / 16.85 / 17.02 / 15.86 | 12.86 / 13.13 / 13.19 / 11.92 |
| expert cache slots, CUDA0/1/2/3 | 6144 / 6656 / 6144 / 5632 | 6144 / 6656 / 6144 / 5632 | 5240 / 5691 / 5557 / 4835 |
| free with everything loaded, MiB, CUDA0/1/2/3 | 1507 / 1601 / 1707 / 1805 | 1325 / 1403 / 2319 / 1639 | 411 / 507 / 507 / 285 |

Free VRAM before the expert cache goes up by 0.58-0.61 GiB per card, a little more than the 0.45-0.48 GiB drop in the engine line. That line counts payload bytes only; I did not look into the difference. On this rig the expert cache already holds every profiled pair, so the slot counts stay the same. The freed VRAM changes what the prompt path borrows instead: on 0.1.45, CUDA0/1/3 lend 324-348 cache slots each to the prompt path and 2.27 GiB of RAM is pinned for them; with the fix every card keeps its own prompt buffers (0.75 GiB each) and nothing is pinned. Those own buffers are new allocations, while the loan reused cache slots, so CUDA0/1/3 end 0.16-0.19 GiB lower with everything loaded, and CUDA2, which had no loan, ends 0.6 GiB higher.

Tokens: `tools/batch_test.py --batch 16 --n 16 --max-new 128 --keys temperature=0 --extra "--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000"`, with the same expert cache on every card in both trimmed arms. 0.1.45 vs fix: solo 16/16 and batch 16/16 identical, and in both arms every slot matches its own solo run. Batch throughput is the same: 236.3 vs 236.4 tok/s; I took no other speed measurement. The no-trim arm has a smaller cache, so its tokens are not compared.

#2427 drops the bf16 copies on a split; this change drops other stages' Q8_0 copies. They change different lines. I did not run them together.

**Not tested:** only CUDA sm_86 was built and run. I have no ROCm, SYCL or Metal toolchain here, so the HIP and Metal builds of this file were not compiled. The two lines only call `outside` and `in_range`, which the same function already calls, so they add no code a backend could fail on. That still leaves the AGENTS.md build rule open, so this stays a draft until someone builds it for HIP. On HIP gfx12 with a UD-* GGUF and stage trim, this should lower VRAM in the same way under the default; the per-card `STRATA_HC_Q8=1: ... GiB` line on an R9700 split would confirm it. The SYCL copy of this loop (`sycl/src/core/native_dense.cpp`) gets the same filter in #2810, so this PR leaves SYCL alone. Also not run: long prompts (the tokens check is 16 short prompts, 128 new tokens, and the prompt path's buffers changed), 2- or 3-GPU splits, `--layer-split auto`, `--keep-canonical`, `STRATA_HC_Q8_INJECT=1`, bf16/GSQ packs, other models.

Folder: `bench/results/2026-10-18-community-rtx-5090-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-s/`.

## What was measured

The official suite (`tools/strata_bench.py`: chat, 4K, 16K, 32K, agent session, 2 short clients) and a long-context extension at about 64K, 128K, 256K, and a full-window prompt of about 511K tokens (the word-list estimate aimed at 523976 and landed short of that). Three runs where the process finished them. Fresh prompts, restored prompts, and two prompts at once are separate rows. Speeds are the engine's timings. A needle check covers 128K, 256K, and 480K at depths 10 and 90. All six were found.

## Limitations worth reading before quoting a number

- A cache hit is a restore in the engine log plus at least 90% of the prompt reused, after both slots were flushed. An immediate resend is not used as the cached condition.
- At 64K and 128K the single-request restore works (time to first token about 0.18 s and 0.26 s). The cached pair restored only one of the two prompts. The restored request decoded at about 33 tok/s with no draft accepts while the other request reread the prompt. That cell is not two cache hits.
- The full-window snapshot was refused on a fresh process: `skip parking (physical RAM admission; need 8243 MiB plus 2560 MiB floor, 9377 MiB available)`. The 16 GiB conversation-cache setting is not the check that fired. The resend read the prompt again.
- The same full-window length inside the long process decoded at about 26 tok/s with 0 draft accepts. A fresh process, with about 193 draft accepts, decoded that length at 180 tok/s (and 236 tok/s on the reread). Those are different rows.
- Two long prefills ran one after the other. The slower time to first token is queueing, not batched decode. There is no parallel-1 arm. YaRN is on for the short rows as well as the long ones.
- `--vram-reserve-mib` stayed 700. Startup reported 119 MiB of VRAM free and suggested a higher reserve.

`long_matrix.py` in the folder is the extension. The official suite is the repository's own tool.

## Title

Issue: Resolves #2331

title: serve: keepawake primes its daemon before the first acquire (a fast request could miss the hold)
body:
## Title
serve: keepawake primes its daemon before the first acquire (a fast request could miss the hold)

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary

`prevent_sleep` starts its worker thread lazily, on the first `acquire`. A request that finishes fast - acquire, then release, all before the thread exists - never reached the loop, so the transient `count > 0` transition was lost and Windows was not held awake for it. The daemon is now started up front, and `acquire` waits until the loop has signalled that it is inside, so no request can outrun the thread.

## What changed

- `serve/keepawake.py` - `_start()` is called at construction, so the daemon waits on the condition from the start; the loop sets `_primed` and notifies under the condition; `acquire` waits on `_primed` before it counts. No public API change, no change to the ON/OFF calls themselves.

## Extra Notes

**Related to #1901, not a duplicate of it:** that PR fixes the same race on the test side, by keeping the mock request generator open until the fake Windows call records ON. This one fixes it in the runtime, which is where a real fast request hits it. The two are complementary; #1901's fixture change is not included here.

**Measured on this PC (Windows, no model loaded, the real power API is not called):**
- `serve/test_keepawake.py`: 6/6 OK, including `test_held_while_busy_and_released_when_idle` and `test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close`.
- Off and non-Windows paths unchanged: `test_off_and_non_windows` and `test_default_service_has_none` pass.

**Not tested:** the real Windows power API (`SetThreadExecutionState`) - forbidden in these tests, as in the existing suite. No suspend/resume behaviour is claimed.

Default path untouched: `prevent_sleep` stays opt-in, and the ON/OFF sequence a held request produces is the same.

## Title
build: pin CMP0169 OLD around FetchContent_Populate (CMake 4.4 warns on every configure)

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary

CMake 4.4 prints an AUTHOR_WARNING on every configure: `Calling FetchContent_Populate(strata_llamacpp) is deprecated` (policy CMP0169, FetchContent.cmake:1968; sites CMakeLists.txt:1461 and sycl/CMakeLists.txt:179). The project's `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)` does not set CMP0169, so it stays OLD and warns; setting it NEW makes the call a FATAL_ERROR. The fix pins the old behaviour, guarded so CMake < 3.30 (no such policy) still configures.

## What changed

- `CMakeLists.txt` - `if(POLICY CMP0169) cmake_policy(SET CMP0169 OLD) endif()` before `FetchContent_Declare`, with the reason in a comment.
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` - the same guarded pin at its FetchContent site.
- `tools/test_fetchcontent_policy.py` - new guard test (unittest, no build, no GPU): every `FetchContent_Populate` call is preceded by the pin, and the pin is guarded, not bare.

## Extra Notes

**Why not `FetchContent_MakeAvailable`** (checked, not assumed): the populate-then-`add_subdirectory` form is deliberate - ggml's binary dir is `/ggml`, the same one the `STRATA_GGML_DIR` branch uses (CMakeLists 1452/1463, sycl 170/181, metal 88). `MakeAvailable` with `SOURCE_SUBDIR ggml` moves it to `_deps/strata_llamacpp-build`, and `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` in `FetchContent_Declare` is only honoured from CMake 3.28 - above this project's 3.24 floor, where it would change the target graph.

title: perf(hip): tune RDNA4 QSA prompt WMMA path (STRATA_HIP_WMMA stays opt-in)
body:
## Summary

Optimizes the HIP `int8`-KV QSA prompt-attention matrix-core kernel (`prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT>` in `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu`).

**`STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` remains opt-in on every architecture (`gfx12` and `gfx11` included).** While this PR's changes inside `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT>` are **100% bitwise identical** to `main`'s `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT>` (`NEWHASH` `2c5cab7eb6601f66` / `deb4f727fbac41af` / `2d10cd9d6d1fd5b5`), the matrix-core path itself differs in its last bits from the default FP32 fallback (`qsa_decode_attn_batch`) due to `FP16 hi + lo` splitting and reduction order. Keeping `STRATA_HIP_WMMA` out of `arch_defaults.cpp` preserves the exact-only policy of `arch_default_env("gfx1201")` and avoids process-wide enablement on `gfx11` stages in mixed-GPU runs.

1. **LDS-only workgroup barriers (`pa_sync_lds`):**
   - Replaces the `__syncthreads()` barriers inside `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel` (which synchronize only LDS `S`) with `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12` and `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx11` (generic `__syncthreads()` elsewhere), avoiding the `s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0` global-load drain and `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` L0 vector-cache invalidation emitted by generic `__syncthreads()` on `gfx12`.
2. **Global-load / WMMA overlap (`fetch` K-before-V + deferred FP16 scale conversion + post-`q·K` V staging):**
   - Keeps `k_scale` and `v_scale` in raw `uint16_t` registers (`Chunk::ksc_u16[2]`, `Chunk::vsc_u16`) during `fetch()` and converts them via `u16_scale()` (with an empty `asm volatile("" : "+v"(u))` barrier on AMDGPU) only at their point of use after the `q·K` WMMAs, preventing LLVM from hoisting `v_cvt_f32_f16` into the conditional global-load blocks and forcing an early `s_wait_loadcnt 0x0`.
   - Issues the `K` global loads before the `V` global loads in `fetch()`, and moves LDS `V` staging (`S.v` / `S.vs`) inside `chunk()` to *after* the `q·K` WMMAs, so `V` global loads stay in flight while the matrix cores compute `q·K`.
3. **Vectorized 32-bit LDS `V` gather + in-register DPP byte transpose (`dpp_tr4`) + VALU wave butterfly reductions (`pa_xor_u32` / `pa_xor_f32`):**
   - Replaces the 64 scalar 1-byte `ds_load_i8` reads per wave per chunk in the `p·V` loop (`S.v[warp][cb + i][d]`) with 16 aligned 32-bit `ds_load_b32` reads (`*reinterpret_cast<const uint32_t*>(&S.v[warp][cb + 4 * q4 + qs4][j * 16 + qm4])`) followed by an in-register 4×4 byte transpose across the 4 lanes of a hardware DPP quad (`dpp_tr4`: `__builtin_amdgcn_mov_dpp` quad_perm `0xb1` / `0x4e` + `__builtin_amdgcn_perm`).
   - Replaces `__shfl_xor_sync` in the `q`-max, row-max, row-sum, `row_x16`, and `V`-scale reductions with VALU lane permutations (`pa_xor_u32` / `pa_xor_f32`: `mov_dpp` quad_perm `0xb1`/`0x4e` for masks `1`/`2`, `permlane16` for `4`/`8`, `permlanex16` for `16`), avoiding `ds_bpermute_b32` traffic through the LDS pipe and cutting `gfx1201` register pressure from `191` to `168` VGPRs (`SPLIT=true`) and `160` to `147` VGPRs (`SPLIT=false`) with `0` spills (`SmemW` remains `21,648 B`).

---

## The change

Three files changed vs `main` (`477ac13c`) at `f9b11142`:

- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu` (+110/−38):
  - Adds `pa_sync_lds()`, `dpp_tr4()`, `pa_xor_u32()`, and `pa_xor_f32()` inside `#if defined(__HIPCC__)`.
  - Updates `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT>`: raw `uint16_t` scales (`Chunk::vsc_u16`, `Chunk::ksc_u16[2]`) + `u16_scale()`, K-before-V global loads in `fetch()`, V slice staged into `S.v`/`S.vs` after the `q·K` WMMAs in `chunk()`, `pa_sync_lds()` barriers, `pa_xor_f32()` butterfly reductions, and aligned 32-bit `S.v` loads + `dpp_tr4()` in `p·V`.
  - `SmemW` layout is unchanged (`uint8_t v[4][WCH][WVS]` with `WVS = 80`, `21,648 B` total).
- `src/core/arch_defaults.cpp` (+2/−0):
  - Comment-only note documenting why `STRATA_HIP_WMMA` is intentionally excluded from the `gfx12` default table.
- `src/core/arch_defaults_test.cpp` (+14/−1):

title: Community benchmark: Apple M4 Pro (48 GB), Flash-Next Q2_0, 262K context streamed from SSD
body:
## Summary
Community benchmark report for the Apple Silicon Metal engine on an **Apple M4 Pro with 48 GB unified memory** — a configuration the docs list as untested (the MAC.md measurements stop at a 32 GB M4 mini and an M5 Max).

- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **Q2_0** (the only size 48 GB fits), **262,144-token context**, experts streamed from SSD (setup's automatic choice + the `.experts` one-request-per-expert copy, `--mmap-experts`, expert cache 64 slots, `--spec 2`).
- Suite: `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1), 3 runs per test, engine-own timings, medians with ranges.

## Results (medians)
| Test | Value |
| --- | --- |
| short chat decode | **26.0 tok/s** (23.0-26.8), TTFT 1.35 s |
| 4K fresh prompt | 247.4 tok/s, TTFT 16.3 s |
| 16K fresh prompt | 280.4 tok/s, TTFT 57.3 s |
| 32K fresh prompt | 280.2 tok/s, TTFT 114.4 s |
| agent session | 68.7 % conversation-cache hit, 5 re-read tokens/session, 24.4 tok/s in-session |

Headline decode lands between the docs' 32 GB M4 mini streaming figures (~14 tok/s) and the M5 Max resident figures (108-120) — on the memory-bandwidth-limited part of the curve, as expected for an SSD-streamed pack on an M4.

## Notes for reviewers
- Engine 0.1.45-metal built **from source** (no ready-made Mac binary exists); upstream HEAD did not compile for Metal without local fixes — details are in the report's *Contributor notes* section (missing Metal-compat shims for #2666's new API, and a stale generated `stubs.cpp`).
- No correctness battery was run (speed-only submission); a real agentic workload on the same install (long-document reading) was noticeably faster end-to-end than the dense 27B it replaced, matching the prefill numbers.
- Results-only PR, no engine changes included (the compat patches are described in prose, not committed here, to keep the report self-contained).

Per docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md's submit-a-report workflow.

title: perf(prefill): port wmma_gemm and gdn_chunked WMMA kernels to RDNA4 gfx12
body:
## Summary

Ports Strata's prefill FP16/BF16 WMMA kernels in `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` and the WY-chunked Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill recurrence in `src/prefill/kernels.cu` (`gdn_chunked`) from RDNA3-only (`gfx11`) to RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`):

1. **Enables `STRATA_WMMA_GFX11=1` for `gfx12` builds (`cmake/hip_backend.cmake:105`):**
   - Previously `cmake/hip_backend.cmake` matched only `gfx11`, so on `gfx1200;gfx1201` builds `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` compiled to `return false;` stubs for `strata_wmma_gemm_f16`, `strata_wmma_gemm_bf16`, `strata_pf_gemm_f16` / `strata_pf_gemm_f16_ld`, `strata_pf_hcdown_bf16`, and `strata_pf_hcdown_exact_bf16`.
2. **Ports `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` to RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`) Wave32 16×16×16 WMMA (P3a):**
   - Extends `strata_wmma_gfx11_device()` to accept `gfx_arch_is_gfx12_wmma()`.
   - Updates `WmmaTraits<_Float16 / __bf16>`, `gemm_wmma_16x16_1w`, `gemm_wmma_64x64_4w`, `pfg::kernel`, `pfg::kernel_bk64` (`STRATA_PF_GEMM=1`), `pfg::kernel_hcdown` (`STRATA_PF_HCDOWN=1`), and `pfg::kernel_hcd_exact` (`STRATA_HCD_EXACT=1`) to use RDNA4 8-element half-wave fragments (`k = 8 * hi + 0..7`), `__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_{f16,bf16}_w32_gfx12`, contiguous half-wave accumulator row mapping (`row = 8 * hi + i`), and LDS-only barriers (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12`, `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx11`).
3. **Ports WY-chunked GDN prefill recurrence (`gdn_wmma_prep_kernel`, `gdn_wmma_scan_kernel`, `gdn_rec_wmma` in `src/prefill/kernels.cu:1513–1875`, `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1`) to RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`):**
   - On `gfx12`, the Wave32 WMMA accumulator layout `(row = 8 * hi + v, col = lane & 15)` is already identical to the B-operand fragment layout `(k = 8 * hi + v, n = lane & 15)`. Converting an accumulator tile `gw_f8` into a B-operand fragment (`gw_acc_to_b`) requires **zero cross-lane permutes** (`4× permlanex16` + `8× v_perm_b32` on `gfx11` become a direct 8-element FP32→FP16 cast on `gfx12`), keeping `gdn_wmma_scan_kernel` at `239 VGPRs` with `0` spills on `gfx1201`.
4. **Fixes host-only BF16 fixture encoding and non-finite checks in `tests/hip/prefill_wmma_gemm_parity.cpp`:**
   - Uses `strata::kernels::bf16_from_f32(value)` in `encode(value, true)` instead of `hip_bfloat16(value).data` (which in a host-only `.cpp` translation unit without `__HIPCC__` performs C++20 parenthesized aggregate initialization `(uint16_t)value` and truncated fractional BF16 inputs to zero), and rejects non-finite `delta` values (`!std::isfinite(delta) || delta > 0.0`).

---

## Root cause

1. **`cmake/hip_backend.cmake:105` & `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu`:**
   - `if(CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES MATCHES "gfx11")` excluded `gfx12`, leaving `STRATA_WMMA_GFX11` undefined on RDNA4 builds so `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` compiled only the `#else` stub section (`return false;`).
   - Within `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu`, device passes checked `#if defined(__gfx1100__) ...` and used RDNA3 16-element replicated fragments (`ext_vector_type(16)`) and interleaved accumulator row indexing (`2 * i + hi`), whereas RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`) Wave32 16×16×16 WMMA instructions (`__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_{f16,bf16}_w32_gfx12`) split the 16-element K-dimension across the two half-waves (`8` elements per lane: `hi = 0` holds `k = 0..7`, `hi = 1` holds `k = 8..15`) and map accumulator elements `c[0..7]` to contiguous half-wave rows `8 * hi + i`.
2. **`src/prefill/kernels.cu:1513–1875` (`gdn_chunked`):**
   - `STRATA_GDN_WMMA` and `gdn_rec_wmma()` checked only `gfx11` targets (`gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma`), so `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1` always returned `false` on `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` and fell back to the token-serial `gdn_rec_fused_kernel`.

---

## The change

- `cmake/hip_backend.cmake`:
  - Match `gfx11|gfx12` when defining `STRATA_WMMA_GFX11=1`.
- `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu`:
  - Define `STRATA_WMMA_DEV_GFX11`, `STRATA_WMMA_DEV_GFX12`, `WMMA_ROW(i, hi)`, `WMMA_K_OFF(hi)`, `wmma_sync_lds()`, and `pfg::pfg_sync_lds()`.
  - Support `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` in `strata_wmma_gfx11_device()`, `WmmaTraits<_Float16>`, `WmmaTraits<__bf16>`, `gemm_wmma_16x16_1w`, `gemm_wmma_64x64_4w`, `pfg::kernel`, `pfg::kernel_bk64`, `pfg::kernel_hcdown`, and `pfg::kernel_hcd_exact`.
- `src/prefill/kernels.cu`:
  - Define `STRATA_GDN_WMMA_GFX11`, `STRATA_GDN_WMMA_GFX12`, and `GW_ROW(v, hi)` for `gdn_wmma_prep_kernel` and `gdn_wmma_scan_kernel`, implement zero-permute `gw_acc_to_b` and `s_wait_dscnt 0x0` barriers on `gfx12`, and allow `gfx_arch_is_gfx12_wmma()` in `gdn_rec_wmma()`.
- `tests/hip/gdn_chunked.cpp` & `tests/hip/prefill_wmma_gemm_parity.cpp`:
  - Enable `gfx_arch_is_gfx12_wmma()` in both test harnesses, fix `encode(value, true)` in `prefill_wmma_gemm_parity.cpp` to use `strata::kernels::bf16_from_f32(value)`, and add exact binary-fraction parity tests (with `!std::isfinite(delta)` guards) for `strata_pf_gemm_f16_ld`, `strata_pf_hcdown_bf16`, and `strata_pf_hcdown_exact_bf16`.

---

### 1. ELF Resource Usage on `gfx1201` (`llvm-readobj --notes`)

Issue: Resolves # (documents #2324)

## Summary

Docs only - no code changed. Two 0.1.44.1 behaviours that no page told:

2. **Setup run again over an installed model keeps its size**: `--setup` opens the size list with the installed size pre-selected, so Enter / `--yes` keep it; a re-run never silently moves a working install to the recommended (slower, larger) size.

## What changed

- `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` - new section for the start crash (#2324): the exit words per OS, the AVX/AVX2/FMA/F16C flags, the `STRATA_ISA_FLOOR` pointer to "Older CPUs".
- `docs/DETAILS.md` - the matching row in the troubleshooting table.
- `docs/INSTALL.md` - the "Running setup again over an installed model?" bullet under "Setup's questions".
- `docs/AI_SETUP.md` - the same re-run rule for an assistant running setup non-interactively.

## Extra Notes

**Verified against the code on `main` (no GPU, no model):**
- #2324 "not retried": `serve/server.py` `engine_crashed` (L475) and the transient-start rule `... and not engine_crashed(rc)` (L562); `serve/test_server.py::StartCrashReported` runs 5/5 OK on Windows (3 skipped, Linux-only signals).
- re-run keeps size: `setup.py` `installed_size` (L2324); `tools/test_setup_rerun_size.py` 8/8 OK.

**Two accuracy fixes vs. the original branch commit, measured against `main`:**
- The AVX/AVX2/FMA/F16C flags are printed only on Linux - `cpu_isa_words()` reads `/proc/cpuinfo` alone, so on Windows/macOS the line names the illegal instruction by itself. The docs say that.
- No reference to the eval harness: `evals/` is not in `main`, so a pointer to it would be a dead link.

Docs only; the default path is untouched.

title: perf(prefill): use single LDS-only barrier per stage in native_w11_kernel
body:
## Summary

Optimizes `native_w11_kernel` (`src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`), the default `gfx12` (`RDNA4`) and opt-in `gfx11` (`STRATA_PF_FUSED=1`) int8-WMMA fused MoE prefill kernel:

1. **Removes the duplicate per-stage barrier (`src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu:913, 964`):**
   - Stage `0`'s decoded weights (`wt[0]`, `ws[0]`) are written by `put(raw, 0)` before the prologue barrier (`line 882`), and each subsequent stage `s + 1`'s decoded weights (`wt[(s + 1) & 1]`, `ws[(s + 1) & 1]`) are written by `put(raw, (s + 1) & 1)` before the end-of-stage barrier added in `#1180` (`line 964`).
   - Because `wt` and `ws` are double-buffered (`wt[2][NW_ROWS][WLD]`, `ws[2][NW_ROWS][4]`), buffer `(s + 1) & 1` is only read in stage `s - 1` (before the barrier at the end of stage `s - 1`). Keeping both the top-of-loop barrier (`line 913`) and the end-of-stage barrier (`line 964`) executed two workgroup barriers per stage (`80` barriers in `GU` across `NS = 40`, `20` in `down` across `NS = 10`) with only `load_unit(s + 2)` and register moves between them.
2. **Replaces full-memory `__syncthreads()` with an LDS-only barrier (`nw_sync_lds()`):**
   - Every barrier in `native_w11_kernel` only synchronizes LDS (`wt`, `ws`, `srow`, `hs`).
   - On HIP, `__syncthreads()` lowers to a workgroup acquire/release fence over all memory (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`, and `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0) lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx11`).
   - Waiting on `loadcnt(0)` / `vmcnt(0)` at every barrier forced `load_unit(s + 2)` and `fetch_b(s + 1)` global loads to complete at the barrier instead of overlapping the next stage's 16 `v_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8` instructions, and `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx12` flushed the L0 vector cache on every stage even though 4 consecutive `GU` stages (`s >> 2`) read sub-blocks from the same 256-value weight superblock.
   - `nw_sync_lds()` uses `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `STRATA_NAT_W11` (matching `gw_lds_barrier()` in `src/prefill/kernels.cu:1572`) and `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `STRATA_NAT_W12`.

---

## Root cause

In `src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu:880–976`:
- Commit `3b499f17` (`#1180`) added `__syncthreads()` after `put(raw, (s + 1) & 1)` at line 964 while leaving the original `__syncthreads()` at the top of `for (int s = 0; s < NS; ++s)` (`line 913`).
- In the `gfx1201` disassembly of `native_w11_kernel<T_IQ3_S, true, true, 8>`:
  - At the end of stage `s`, `put(raw, (s + 1) & 1)` stored to LDS and executed `s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait 0xffff; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` (`line 964`).
  - Immediately after, `load_unit(s + 2)` issued 5 `global_load` instructions for stage `s + 2`'s compressed weights, and the loop backedge immediately hit the second `__syncthreads()` (`line 913`), emitting `s_wait_loadcnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait 0xffff; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` — stalling on `load_unit(s + 2)` and invalidating the L0 vector cache before stage `s + 1`'s WMMAs began.

---

## The change

- `src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`:
  - Define `nw_sync_lds()` (`s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)\n\ts_barrier` on `STRATA_NAT_W11`, `s_wait_dscnt 0x0\n\ts_barrier_signal -1\n\ts_barrier_wait -1` on `STRATA_NAT_W12`, `__syncthreads()` fallback).
  - Remove the redundant top-of-loop barrier at the start of `for (int s = 0; s < NS; ++s)` and replace the remaining `__syncthreads()` calls in `native_w11_kernel` with `nw_sync_lds()`.

---

## Evidence

### 1. `gfx1201` Disassembly Verification (`llvm-objdump -d`)

- Eliminates all `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` instructions from `native_w11_kernel` (previously `82` L0 cache invalidations per 64-row tile in `GU` and `22` in `down`).
- Halves per-stage barrier count (`80 → 39` in `GU`, `20 → 9` in `down`).
- In the steady-state stage loop (`s = 1..NS-2`), `fetch_b(s + 1)`'s 10 `global_load_b64` instructions execute concurrently with all 16 `v_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8` instructions of stage `s` with zero `s_wait_loadcnt` instructions inside the WMMA loop body.

### 2. Bitwise Parity & Single-Layer Prefill Benchmark (`hip_prefill_fused_iq`, `S20_NOMMQ=1`, 3 alternating rounds × 8 back-to-back runs per round on `gfx1201`)
